blocks.html: Nor could one personally [unclear: perſonnément, as printed — Middle French personnement, "in person, personally", which Ringold–Lewis also read; or a misprint for pertinemment] found oneself upon the knowledge which the prisoner had of all those whom he met the first time: for besides the magic, of which he was strongly suspected, he has since confessed, at the execution, that certain persons had given him certain information and advice. Still less can one make use of the likeness of the said Martin's sisters to the said prisoner; because, as has often been said, judgment by likeness is not sure — of which several examples could be cited.
